items.title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids
items.content:
Extreme space-weather events can damage power systems on Earth and degrade GPS accuracy and satellite operations. A new machine learning system can predict where damage is likely to occur 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives.

The post Forecasting space weather risks on power grids appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Extreme space-weather events can damage power systems on Earth and degrade GPS accuracy and satellite operations. A new machine learning system can predict where damage is likely to occur 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives.
The post Forecasting space weather risks on power grids appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Rohan Kannan

summaries.zh: 极端空间天气事件可能损害地球电力系统，降低GPS精度并影响卫星运行。一种新的机器学习系统能在风暴来临前30-60分钟预测潜在损害地点。该研究由微软研究院发布。
summaries.en: Extreme space-weather events pose risks to power grids, GPS accuracy, and satellite operations. A new machine learning system developed by Microsoft Research can predict potential damage locations 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives, enhancing early warning capabilities. The system aims to mitigate the impact of space weather on critical infrastructure.

items.title: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology
items.content:
Biology doesn't operate in silos, and neither should the AI representation of it. Quine is an early-stage research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology. By connecting insights across biological scales and modalities, Quine helps scientists computationally search a space far larger than intuition allows and prioritize hypotheses before they reach the lab. Experimental results provide important feedback, helping researchers sharpen future research directions.

The post Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Biology doesn't operate in silos, and neither should the AI representation of it. Quine is an early-stage research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology. By connecting insights across biological scales and modalities, Quine helps scientists computationally search a space far larger than intuition allows and prioritize hypotheses before they reach the lab. Experimental results provide important feedback, helping researchers sharpen future research directions.
The post Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Nicolo Fusi, Jonathan M. Carlson

summaries.zh: Quine是一款专为生物学复杂性设计的AI研究系统。该系统旨在构建多模态生物学世界模型，通过整合不同尺度和模态的生物学见解，帮助科学家在直觉难以覆盖的广阔空间中进行计算搜索，并在实验前优先排序假设。实验结果为研究人员提供重要反馈，以优化未来研究方向。Quine由微软研究院开发，旨在打破生物学研究的孤立状态。
summaries.en: Quine is an AI research system developed by Microsoft Research to model the complexity of biology. It creates a multimodal world model by integrating insights across different biological scales and modalities. Quine enables scientists to computationally search vast hypothesis spaces and prioritize research before experimentation. Experimental feedback is used to refine future research directions, enhancing the efficiency of biological studies. The system aims to bridge gaps in biological understanding by connecting diverse data types.

items.title: Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics
items.content:
Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads.

The post Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads.
The post Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Ganesh Ananthanarayanan, Matthew Balkwill, Xenofon Foukas, Sanjeev Mehrotra, Bozidar Radunovic, Connor Settle, Ankit Verma, David White, Shawn Cicoria, Mark Martin, Rachel Johnson, Mayur Patel

summaries.zh: 微软研究院研究发现，将AI推理任务从机器人硬件中卸载到外部设备，可提升任务成功率、提高效率，并支持更复杂的物理AI应用。这一技术有助于缓解机器人硬件与AI智能发展不匹配的问题，推动物理AI在现实场景中的进步。
summaries.en: Microsoft Research finds that offloading AI inference to external hardware enhances robot performance, efficiency, and supports advanced physical AI tasks. This approach allows robots to handle more complex workloads while improving task success.

items.title: Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera
items.content:
Custom-made molecules are advancing medicine, materials, and agriculture, but producing them is slow and expensive. A new Nature paper highlights RetroChimera, a predictive model that helps accelerate chemical synthesis, helping researchers explore a wide range of molecules.

The post Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Custom-made molecules are advancing medicine, materials, and agriculture, but producing them is slow and expensive. A new Nature paper highlights RetroChimera, a predictive model that helps accelerate chemical synthesis, helping researchers explore a wide range of molecules.
The post Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Felix Pultar, John Gardner, Guoqing Liu, Marwin Segler

summaries.zh: 《Nature》杂志发表的一篇新论文介绍了RetroChimera，一种预测模型，旨在加速小分子的化学合成。该模型有助于研究人员探索多种分子，从而推动药物、材料和农业领域的创新。RetroChimera通过提高合成预测的准确性，降低了定制分子的生产成本和时间，为科研提供了重要工具。
summaries.en: RetroChimera, a predictive model developed by Microsoft Research, is featured in a Nature paper for accelerating small-molecule synthesis. It helps researchers explore diverse molecules by improving synthesis prediction at scale, addressing the slow and costly production of custom-made molecules used in medicine, materials, and agriculture. The model enhances efficiency in chemical research.

items.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models
items.content:
What if pathology foundation models could do more with less? GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash cut computational demands while maintaining strong performance, opening the door to larger studies and broader exploration.

The post GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
What if pathology foundation models could do more with less? GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash cut computational demands while maintaining strong performance, opening the door to larger studies and broader exploration.
The post GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Naoto Usuyama, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Tristan Naumann

summaries.zh: GigaPath-Flash和GigaTIME-Flash是高效的病理基础模型，通过降低计算需求同时保持高性能，为大规模研究提供了可能。这些模型有助于更广泛的病理学探索，推动群体层面的发现。
summaries.en: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash are efficient pathology foundation models developed by Microsoft Research. These models reduce computational demands while maintaining strong performance, enabling larger-scale studies and broader exploration. They aim to advance population-scale discovery in pathology by optimizing resource usage without sacrificing accuracy. The innovations in these models facilitate more extensive research and analysis in the field.

items.title: Broadening access to Skala creates a faster path to predictive DFT
items.content:
Skala 1.1, the updated deep-learning exchange-correlation functional from Microsoft Research, provides greater accuracy, expanded accessibility across the computational chemistry ecosystem, and a living benchmark to track computational performance.

The post Broadening access to Skala creates a faster path to predictive DFT  appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Skala 1.1, the updated deep-learning exchange-correlation functional from Microsoft Research, provides greater accuracy, expanded accessibility across the computational chemistry ecosystem, and a living benchmark to track computational performance. 
The post Broadening access to Skala creates a faster path to predictive DFT  appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Sebastian Ehlert, Stefano Battaglia, Thijs Vogels, Jan Hermann, Jens Wehner, Giulia Luise, Klaas Giesbertz, Chin-Wei Huang, Aaron Kaplan, Kate Milton, Stephanie Marisa Lanius, Derk Kooi, P. Bernát Szabó, Gregor Simm, Rianne van den Berg, Paola Gori Giorgi

summaries.zh: 微软研究院发布的深度学习交换关联函数更新版Skala 1.1，提高了精度，扩展了计算化学生态系统的可访问性，并作为动态基准来追踪计算性能。该更新有助于加速预测性密度泛函理论的发展。
summaries.en: Skala 1.1, an updated deep-learning exchange-correlation functional from Microsoft Research, enhances accuracy and expands accessibility within the computational chemistry ecosystem. It serves as a living benchmark to monitor performance, facilitating faster progress toward predictive density functional theory (DFT). The release aims to improve widespread adoption and efficiency in computational chemistry.

items.title: MindTopo reveals VLMs’ spatial reasoning abilities
items.content:
A path, a fence, a knot. MindTopo sets a new benchmark for testing how AI understands topological relationships and highlights new opportunities to strengthen spatial reasoning and planning.

The post MindTopo reveals VLMs’ spatial reasoning abilities appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
A path, a fence, a knot. MindTopo sets a new benchmark for testing how AI understands topological relationships and  highlights new opportunities to strengthen spatial reasoning and planning.
The post MindTopo reveals VLMs’ spatial reasoning abilities appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Yunfei Ge, Anbang Liu, Qineng Wang, Johnalbert Garnica, Zihan Wang, Reuben Tan, Jianfeng Gao, Ruohan Zhang, Yining Hong, Jiajun Wu, Manling Li

summaries.zh: MindTopo通过测试路径、栅栏和结等拓扑关系，展示了视觉语言模型（VLMs）的空间推理能力，为提升AI的空间推理和规划能力提供了新方向。该成果由微软研究院发布。
summaries.en: MindTopo has established a new benchmark for evaluating how AI systems understand topological relationships. The tool highlights advancements in spatial reasoning and planning for Vision-Language Models (VLMs). It demonstrates the potential to enhance AI's ability to interpret spatial contexts, such as identifying paths, fences, and knots. The findings are presented by Microsoft Research.

items.title: Introducing CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement
items.content:
Radiology AI is evolving beyond report generation. CARE-X explores a unified approach that combines flexible reasoning, calibrated predictions, and measurement-based tools for chest X-ray interpretation.

The post Introducing CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Radiology AI is evolving beyond report generation. CARE-X explores a unified approach that combines flexible reasoning, calibrated predictions, and measurement-based tools for chest X-ray interpretation.
The post Introducing CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Mercy Ranjit, Nikhilesh E, Dr. Abhyuday Kumara  Swamy, Tanuja Ganu

summaries.zh: CARE-X 是一种面向临床应用的放射学视觉语言模型（VLM）。该模型结合了灵活推理、校准预测和工具增强测量，用于胸部X光片解读。它采用辅助监督、奖励对齐学习等方法，提升模型在放射学领域的实用性和准确性。该研究成果由微软研究院发布。
summaries.en: CARE-X is an advanced radiology AI system designed for chest X-ray interpretation, moving beyond simple report generation. It integrates flexible reasoning, calibrated predictions, and tool-augmented measurement. The system employs auxiliary supervision and reward-aligned learning to enhance clinical utility. Developed by Microsoft Research, CARE-X aims to improve the accuracy and reliability of radiology virtual learning models.

items.title: Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI
items.content:
Orchard is an open-source framework for the research community to train and evaluate AI agents across task types. It reduces complexity while supporting strong performance from smaller models by enabling researchers to reuse the same infrastructure.

The post Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.contentSnippet:
Orchard is an open-source framework for the research community to train and evaluate AI agents across task types. It reduces complexity while supporting strong performance from smaller models by enabling researchers to reuse the same infrastructure.
The post Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI appeared first on Microsoft Research.
items.creator: Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Qianhui Wu, Hao Cheng, Jianfeng Gao

summaries.zh: Orchard是一个开源框架，旨在帮助研究社区训练和评估不同任务类型的AI智能体。该框架简化了操作流程，通过复用基础设施，使小型模型也能实现高性能。该框架由微软研究院开发，可用于推动可扩展的智能体AI研究。
summaries.en: Orchard is an open-source framework designed for training and evaluating AI agents across various tasks. It simplifies complexity while enabling strong performance from smaller models by allowing researchers to reuse infrastructure. The framework aims to support scalable agentic AI research. (Word count: 50)
